address: 25 St James Place West, Plymouth PL1 3AT (ground floor flat)
lead_profile_text: Existing property switching from long-let to short-term let - inherited, 'accidental landlord'
stl_goal: Higher returns, more control, avoid Section 21 removal and problem-tenant risk
property_situation: Ground floor flat in a converted house split into two 2-bed flats (brother owns the top floor; 50/50 freehold, both on the lease). Currently long-let at £1,200-£1,300/month. Mortgage renewal late Feb 2027 at ~5.5% (~£450/month); sole trader. Refurb underway, finishing early 2027 (start of spring at latest). Sleeps up to 6. Also owns long-lets in Gosport that he sees as long-let only.
property_type: 2-bed ground floor flat in converted period house (freehold share and lease), near Plymouth Hoe
primary_blocker: Three sequential external gates: his brother (co-freeholder, they have fallen out) and the lease, a holiday-let mortgage at the late-Feb renewal, and refurb completion

meeting_flow.opening_phrase: And then we go through figures and our service.
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: Right, I see. Okay, all right, well, I've got the figures. What I'll do, I'll share my screen and we can go through some figures.
meeting_flow.income_intro: So about £57,000 of gross revenue ... looking at about sort of £2,500 per month, about £30,000-ish a year.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: Yeah, exactly. So we charge 15% plus VAT and that will cover a few different things.
meeting_flow.pre_close_setup: Obviously I've just gone through a lot, or does it work? I mean, is that profitable for you based off of the mortgage renewal that you're looking at?
meeting_flow.close_phrase: What I'll do from here, Ryan, is I'll send you just like a summary of everything we've spoken about ... an action plan in it as well so you can see what you can expect first year, second year.
meeting_flow.meeting_2_ask: I'll probably touch base sort of end of Feb time, see if everything's still on the cards.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Is that the £30 grand after your commissions, or is that on average what you'd probably make?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: That's after the commission. The only thing to pay is mortgage and bills.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: If that was a figure more or less on the mark, then yeah, it would be ... at the moment I'm looking at around £1,200 to £1,300 for a long-term let per month, and the mortgage on renewal is around 5.5%, so it's going to be nearly £450 a month.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: If it was 20% off I'd be surprised; even 30% off, based off what you're saying, it's still the better option.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: if at a profit margin like this, then yeah, it definitely would be more attractive for me, to go this route.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Am I supposed to notify him of changes that I'm making ... so I don't have to notify the local authority or the other freeholder?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: No licence needed and nothing to stop you, but you would have to notify the other freeholder; with 50/50 split I'm not entirely sure what happens if he says no; frame it as an opportunity for his flat too.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: I did think that, yeah, because he's gonna suffer with the same problem basically.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I guess it's a full service that you sign up for, is it? ... which covers the management, the cleaning, the maintenance and whatever else.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: 15% plus VAT covers multi-platform listing, dynamic pricing, guest screening and deposits, cleaning and maintenance coordination; lead handles mortgage, bills and compliance; calendar, Slack and monthly statement with payout 1st-5th.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Is this all tax deductible as well? ... I'm a sole trader at the moment.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Costs are deductible; you pay tax on the net payout; mortgage interest deductibility is different for a sole trader than a limited company.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: When was the company established? ... how many clients do you have? ... how do you set up a network in Plymouth to get that rolling?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Airbnb since 2020, managing for others since summer 2023, ~70 properties nationwide, team of about 8; nationwide trade framework of vetted cleaners, locksmiths, electricians and plumbers; business partner runs operations from Leeds.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Oh, you built the network? Oh, okay.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I know some tradesmen, plumber for instance ... would I be able to reduce some of the fee if I use my own?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: Yes - no problem using your own trades or cleaner as long as they are quality; can coordinate by message or speak to them on your behalf.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Yeah, that's a fair point because obviously it affects reviews and experiences.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: I've used Airbnb a lot over the years. I've never experienced I've had to pay a deposit before. Do you not think that would scare some people off?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: It only scares off people with bad intentions; £350-£400 refundable deposit plus ID check; platform insurance covers serious damage (used once in 6 years - a kitchen fire).

lead_responses.what_lead_said: Is that something you're familiar with? ... I assume I need to change the head lease.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: First thing is to mention it to your brother; if he agrees, get the lease changed - not really a big job; even if you don't change it, everyone bound by the lease is in agreement so nobody's going to pull you up on it.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Yeah, that's what I thought. Yeah, yeah.

conversion_gaps.gap: Legal and consent advice was given too loosely: 'you don't have to notify anyone' then 'you would have to notify the other freeholder'; 'nobody's going to pull you up' on not changing the lease
conversion_gaps.evidence: "You don't have to notify anyone that you've changed the property to a short-term let." ... "even if you don't change it, ... it's not like anyone's going to pull you up on it."
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Correct in the follow-up: co-freeholder agreement, lease check and deed of variation, lender consent or holiday-let mortgage, short-let buildings insurance

conversion_gaps.gap: Income presented as £2,500/month while the deck's own forecast array totals ~£25,968 (£2,164/month); sharp January trough (£231) and December peak looked unreliable
conversion_gaps.evidence: "I think this is probably a little bit off. I don't think it will go this low personally. I think this is just the data skewing things."
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Use the forecast array total and disclose the difference; present Year 1 at roughly 80%

conversion_gaps.gap: Tax answer was incorrect or confused for a sole trader (FHL regime ended April 2025; individuals get a 20% credit on mortgage interest, not full deduction)
conversion_gaps.evidence: "if it's interest-only mortgage, so should the mortgage as well if you've got it in a limited company"
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Correct in the email and suggest he confirms with his accountant

conversion_gaps.gap: Brother relationship (fallen out, equal authority) is the real blocker and Zac admitted not knowing what happens if he says no
conversion_gaps.evidence: Zac: "I'm not entirely sure, if I'm honest." Lead: "And we have actually fallen out"
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Provide a short brief he can share with his brother showing the benefit to the top flat, and signpost legal advice on the lease

conversion_gaps.gap: Holiday-let mortgage and timing coordination at the late-Feb renewal not discussed in detail
conversion_gaps.evidence: "on top of getting a holiday let mortgage"; "I'm trying to decide on a deal at the moment, but the rates keep on changing weekly"
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Offer the short-let income letter for lenders and a call before renewal; touch base 22 Feb 2027
